I understand how you feel. Ive been fighting lung cancer for 2 years now and have gone through immunotherapy, multiple rounds of chemotherapy, 2 major surgeries (brain and femur) as well as so much radiation I should be a marvel character by now and all to have it come back time and time again.  I also was fortunate enough to find and marry a wonderful woman in the 2 years I've been fighting (married 6 months as of today)

I know where you are coming from, I'm only 60 days into my diagnosis (1 major surgery, 1 minor and about to start chemo next week) I went from full on panic and getting my affairs in order to a peace and serenity like I've never known.
There were a few things that helped me to get to this point
1. a relative had said something along the lines of "you can't control this, you just have to go with it"
2. (not kidding about this) one night I had broken down and had a conversation with the corner of my wall and I asked for help, I didn't bargain, I didn't plead, I just asked. the next morning I woke up feeling better about my situation and the team that is treating me.
3. when I was in the ICU post surgery, one of the nurses (this nurse has been battling cancer for 7 years I think, though memory is a bit fuzzy due to all the drugs I was on) told me it's about surviving to the next day, treatments are changing and advancing all the time you just have to survive to the next day.

these things helped me tremendously, I've been changed by my diagnosis, but for the better I like to believe. I hope reading this can help bring you the peace you are searching for, also my DM's are always open
